name: Tooltip
description:
A short label for a control, shown on hover and keyboard focus after 500ms. It composes
with other triggers in either direction:

  <Tooltip content="More actions"><Menu.Trigger render={<Button … />} /></Tooltip>
  <Menu.Trigger render={<Tooltip content="More actions"><Button … /></Tooltip>} />

The trigger keeps its own accessible name; the tooltip repeats it visually.
signature: ({ side, align, enabled, arrow, ...props }: TooltipProps): import("react").JSX.Element

props.name: align
props.description: Alignment of the overlay relative to its anchor.

props.name: arrow
props.description: A pointer towards the trigger. On by default: tooltips label small, similar targets.

props.name: children
props.description:
The element the tooltip describes. No wrapper is added: the trigger's props and ref are
merged onto it, so it must forward its ref and spread props (every design-system control does).
A disabled control must stay hoverable — render it with aria-disabled
(Base UI `focusableWhenDisabled`) rather than the native disabled attribute.

props.name: content
props.description: One line: the control's name, or why it is disabled. Never interactive content (R13.5).

props.name: describe
props.description:
Link the open tooltip to the trigger with aria-describedby. Default: only when the
content is text that differs from the trigger's aria-label (a reason, extra detail) —
a tooltip that repeats the name would be announced twice.

props.name: enabled
props.description: Set false to suppress the tooltip (for example while text is not truncated).

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the next open state when the tooltip shows (hover or focus, after the delay) or hides. Pair with `open` to control it.

props.name: open
props.description: Controls whether the overlay is open.

props.name: shortcut
props.description: A keyboard shortcut drawn after the text in keycaps ("mod+k").

props.name: side
props.description:
Preferred side of the anchor; collision handling may choose another side. The logical
`inline-start` and `inline-end` follow the writing direction (a menu row's reason uses
`inline-end`, beside the menu).

props.name: className
props.description:
CSS class applied to the element, or a function that
returns a class based on the component's state.

props.name: closeOnClick
props.description: Whether the tooltip should close when this trigger is clicked.

props.name: handle
props.description: A handle to associate the trigger with a tooltip.

props.name: name
props.description: The component’s name or native form field name, as specified by its value type.

props.name: payload
props.description: A payload to pass to the tooltip when it is opened.

props.name: ref
props.type: ((((instance: HTMLButtonElement | null) => void | (() => VoidOrUndefinedOnly) | DO_NOT_USE_OR_YOU_WILL_BE_FIRED_CALLBACK_REF_RETURN_VALUES[keyof DO_NOT_USE_OR_YOU_WILL_BE_FIRED_CALLBACK_REF_RETURN_VALUES]) | RefObject<HTMLButtonElement | null>) & (((instance: HTMLElement | null) => void | (() => VoidOrUndefinedOnly) | DO_NOT_USE_OR_YOU_WILL_BE_FIRED_CALLBACK_REF_RETURN_VALUES[keyof DO_NOT_USE_OR_YOU_WILL_BE_FIRED_CALLBACK_REF_RETURN_VALUES]) | RefObject<HTMLElement | null>)) | null | undefined
props.description:
Allows getting a ref to the component instance.
Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null`
(or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).

props.name: style
props.description:
Style applied to the element, or a function that
returns a style object based on the component's state.

props.name: value
props.description: The controlled value. Keep it in application state and update it in the change callback.
